name: AdenNet core network / server facility (Aden)
notes: Control side: IRG/Aden. AdenNet created June 2018 by the internationally recognized government as the alternative ISP to Houthi-controlled YemenNet; RIPE member record (A-grade registration, Al-Mulla Main Street, Aden, PO Box 1221) and AS204317 (PeeringDB) confirm network infrastructure in Aden; customer portal active. Network-level evidence is A; a named physical data center remains a B lead - no official facility page found this run.

name: TeleYemen Aden international gateway and cable landing station (Aden-Djibouti, AAE-1)
notes: Control side: IRG/STC-held Aden. TeleYemen official statement: AAE-1 landing station in Aden with TeleYemen capacity, investment up to ~US$40M (A-grade for gateway/cable-landing facts); Aden also lands Aden-Djibouti cable (1994, owners include TeleYemen per GeoCables; IRG government activated it for south Yemen late 2022 per ts2.tech). Gateway/hosting service = A; cable status volatile: Red Sea cable incidents 2024-2025 and a dual-authority dispute over TeleYemen representation on AAE-1 (IRG refusing Houthi-linked arm) keep AAE-1 status uncertain. Not a commercial colocation DC.

name: PM Bin Brik Aden telecom modernization plan (lead signal)
developer: MTIT (IRG, Aden) under PM Bin Brik
notes: Control side: IRG/Aden. PM Bin Brik directed an urgent Aden telecom-modernization plan on 2025-06-22 (Yemen Monitor 143571, per YE methodology). Plan-level signal for future telecom/data-center infrastructure in Aden; no facility-level evidence or DC component publicly named yet.

name: TeleYemen Mukalla/Seiyun branch presence
notes: Control side: southern coast (IRG-affiliated administration in Mukalla). TeleYemen official contact page lists Mukalla Branch (Khor Almukalla, 26th Sept) and Seiyun presence (A for branch fact); institutional gateway/telecom presence only, not a public DC. AdenNet Phase 2 (2024) network coverage also extends to Hadhramaut per methodology/Barran lead (B, network-level). No named data-center facility found in Mukalla/Seiyun; oil-sector and Hadhramout University server rooms are C-grade at best and unnamed.

name: FALCON submarine cable landing station, Al Hudaydah (TeleYemen)
notes: Control side: Ansar Allah (Houthi)-held Al Hudaydah; IRG contests. Landing station existence = B/A (Submarine Networks lists TeleYemen Al Hudaydah cable landing station for FALCON). Status is volatile and war-affected: Jan 2022 Saudi-led airstrikes damaged the TeleYemen telecom building in Hodeidah causing a nationwide internet outage (antiwar.com 2022-01-20); Jul 2023 TeleYemen condemned targeting of its Al Hudaydah telecommunications building (teleyemen.co); 2024-2025 Red Sea cable incidents keep status uncertain. Do not mark operational without a fresh dated source; not a commercial DC.

name: TeleYemen Hodeidah branch
notes: Control side: Ansar Allah-held Hodeidah. TeleYemen official contact page lists the Hodeidah branch (Al-Muwaslat Street, PO Box 3429-Hodeidah) - A for branch presence. Branch/telecom presence only; no public data-center facility.
